newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Justice Dept appeals tobacco advertising case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Justice Dept appeals tobacco advertising case.

text.p: The U.S. Justice Department on Friday appealed a federal judge's ruling that the Food and Drug Administration cannot regulate cigarette advertising and promotions, President Bill Clinton said.
"The Department is asking for an expedited appeal, because every day of delay matters to our children's health," Clinton said in a statement.

Clinton had announced his intention to make the appeal on April 25, the day the ruling was issued by U.S. District Court Judge William Osteen. Osteen ruled in North Carolina that the FDA does not have the authority to regulate cigarette advertising and promotions.
Major U.S. tobacco companies said on Thursday they intended to appeal a separate part of the ruling that said the FDA had the power to regulate cigarettes and other products containing nicotine.
